source: Socratic-SWE: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Trace-Derived Agent Skills
summary: Closed-loop self-evolution framework that distills historical solving traces into structured agent skills (recurring failure patterns + repair strategies), then injects them into future prompts. Achieves 50.40% on SWE-bench Verified after 3 iterations.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses the 'no agent memory across runs' limitation; skill hints can be injected into Planning/Implementing prompts via promptRenderer.ts

source: RL for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces (arXiv:2605.02801)
summary: Formalizes orchestration learning as five sub-decisions (spawn, delegate, communicate, aggregate, stop); shows that per-stage telemetry traces are the substrate needed for RL-based policy optimization. Connects to Kimi Agent Swarm, OpenAI Codex, and Claude Code case studies.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge has no per-stage telemetry; adding StageExecution metrics creates the data substrate for future RL-based routing decisions

summary: LangGraph's v1.1 production release added configurable retry middleware with exponential backoff and content moderation middleware; demonstrates the pattern is production-proven for agent subprocess invocations.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge enters AIBlocked immediately on any subprocess failure; adding retry with failure classification eliminates false escalations from transient errors

source: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents (arXiv:2606.30306)
summary: Survey establishing that persistent agent orchestration requires formal failure governance distinguishing transient from semantic failures to avoid infinite retry loops and premature escalation. June 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — supporting reference for HID-167 failure classification taxonomy; provides the theoretical grounding for transient/semantic/fatal failure categories

summary: March 2026 paper from Shanghai Jiao Tong + Microsoft Research; mines recurring tool-call patterns from traces and pre-executes likely next tools speculatively, achieving 48.5% reduction in task completion time and 1.8x throughput improvement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — designed for lightweight LLM tool calls; AgentForge's 'tools' are full subprocess invocations (Claude Code, Codex) making direct application expensive. A speculative plan-branching variant is possible but requires parallel subprocess management not in scope.

summary: 630-line Python framework released March 2026 where AI agents autonomously run ML experiments (propose-train-evaluate loop) overnight. Gained 66k+ stars. Primary use case is training improvement, not software engineering orchestration.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the propose-evaluate loop is inspiring for plan-revision self-improvement, but AutoResearch targets ML experiment search not code issue resolution; domain mismatch reduces direct applicability.

source: AdaptFlow: Adaptive Workflow Optimization via Meta-Learning (arXiv:2508.08053)
summary: EMNLP 2025 paper; MAML-inspired bi-level optimization that learns a generalizable workflow initialization and adapts it per-subtask via LLM-generated feedback. Inner loop refines for specific subtask, outer loop generalizes across task families.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — concept of meta-learning workflow initialization is relevant to AgentForge's static state machine, but paper is August 2025 (pre-cutoff) and the bi-level optimization requires rewriting stage sequencing logic — high feasibility cost for uncertain gain.

source: TOKI: Bitemporal Operator Algebra for Contradiction Resolution in LLM-Agent Persistent Memory (arXiv:2606.06240)
summary: June 2026 paper formalizing contradiction resolution in agent persistent memory as write-time concurrency control; introduces bitemporal operators (last-writer-wins, evidence-weighted merge, await-confirmation) with isolation preconditions.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge has no persistent cross-run memory yet; this is highly relevant only after HID-165 (skill hint storage) is implemented. Premature to tackle contradiction resolution before the base memory layer exists.

source: Zylos Research: Speculative Execution and Parallel Tool Calling (April 2026)
summary: Research blog covering parallel tool calling patterns showing 1.8x-3.7x wall-clock speedups and up to 6x cost reductions; references PASTE and LangGraph fan-out/fan-in via Send edges.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — valuable framework survey but the patterns require lightweight tool calls, not full subprocess agents; AgentForge's single-agent-per-stage model would need architectural changes for parallel execution.

source: Mem0 State of AI Agent Memory 2026 Report
summary: Industry benchmark report consolidating three-tier memory taxonomy (episodic, semantic, procedural) and multi-signal retrieval (semantic similarity + BM25 + entity matching fusion). 3-4x token cost reduction from memory-compressed context.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — foundational reference for future memory architecture but too broad; specific patterns (vector search, BM25 fusion) are better addressed after a basic AgentSkillHint layer (HID-165) proves value.
